title: Father of Light! Conduct Our Feet
description: Father of Light! Conduct Our Feet in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Christopher Smart wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 37, “Prayer for Wisdom”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of light! con-duct our feet Through life's dark, dan-gerous road; Let each ad-vanc-ing step still bring Us near-er to our God.

lines: Father of light! conduct our feet
Let each advancing step still bring
Let heaven-eyed prudence be our guide;
Recall our feet from folly's paths
And let it guard, and guide, and warm,
Till it shall lead us to Thyself,
And all our darkness be dispersed

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Christopher Smart died in 1771.
credits: Words by Christopher Smart (1722–1771), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
